newsitem.title: USA: Stocks, bonds edge lower; dollar mixed.
newsitem.headline: Stocks, bonds edge lower; dollar mixed.

text.p: Stock prices fell Monday as investors took a breather after the market raced to four new highs last week. Bonds edged lower and the dollar ended mixed.
Wheat prices tumbled on worries about exports. Crude oil ended higher.
The Dow Jones industrial average fell 3.36 points to 6,090.87 after soaring 125 points last week, ending with a record high close Friday of 6,094.23.
In the broader market, declining issues led advances 1,306 to 1,057 on heavy volume of 414 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange.

"It's a fairly quiet week for economic news so it's the quarterly earnings and comments surrounding them that are the news," said Charlie Crane, director of research of Spears Benzak Salomon & Farrell.
The market lurched along in fits and starts from the opening, as investors reacted to third-quarter results from International Business Machines Corp.
"The market followed IBM. It is certainly a bellwether not just for the tech sector but for corporate America," Crane said.
The Dow index topped 6,100 for the first time during the session, hitting a high of 6,133.73 before touching a low of 6,059.94 as investors cashed out some profits.
Likewise, IBM ended up 75 cents at $130.125 after hitting a 52-week high of $135.375 vs. a session low of $126.75.
IBM said it earned $1.3 billion in the third quarter vs. a loss of $500 million a year ago when it was paying for its acquisition of Lotus Development Corp.
Just as IBM set the tone for trading on Monday, computer software giant Microsoft could set Tuesday's pace.
After the market closed on Monday, Microsoft said its quarterly earnings rose to a record $614 million from $499 million in the year-ago quarter. The earnings topped Wall Street estimates.
The 30-year Treasury bond fell 3/32, or 93.75 cents on a $1,000 bond, raising its yield to 6.81 percent from 6.80 percent late on Friday.

In currency markets, the dollar rose to 112.72 Japanese yen from 112.57 late on Friday, after hitting 112.90 yen, the highest since 113.58 in January 1994. The dollar fell to 1.5352 German marks from 1.5420 on Friday.
Wheat prices tumbled as the United States struggled to compete with rival exporters amid talk its supplies were overpriced.
Wheat for December delivery fell as low as $4 a bushel at the Chicago Board of Trade, the lowest price since June 1995. It closed 4-1/4 cents lower at $4.00-1/2 a bushel.
November crude oil rose 13 cents to $25.92 a barrel at the New York Mercantile Exchange.
December gold added $1.80 to $383.90 an ounce on New York's Commodity Exchange.
Overseas, British stocks hit a record, with the FTSE 100 index rising 20 points to 4,073.1. Tokyo's benchmark Nikkei 225 average sank 309.35 points to 21,302.95.
